coaching.title: Easy 3 mi Z2 + Strength
coaching.message: Travel day (JFK to San Salvador), so keep this honest and easy: 3 flat miles in Zone 2, HR 138-150, fully conversational. If you land before running, do it after you settle to shake out the flight. Pair it with today's strength block: eccentric/plyometric durability — slow-tempo split squats, controlled step-downs, calf eccentrics, low box hops, plus core. That descending-load work is exactly what saves your quads on the Julian Alps 2500m of vert. 48 days out, we're in peak build — the calendar is easing you in, so don't add mileage.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Short easy session needs no special fueling, but a travel day does. Airport and airline food will spike sodium and stall hydration — bring water, aim for 500ml/hr in transit, and pack a real carb+protein option (rice bowl, jerky, fruit) so you're not landing depleted. Post-run, hit your ~30g protein recovery window to support the eccentric strength work. Keep total carbs solid today (~220g) since tomorrow's training builds on this.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Flying compresses recovery — cabin pressure and sitting reduce circulation right when your legs are absorbing plyometric load. Get up and walk the aisle every hour, do ankle pumps at your seat, and compression socks are worth it today. On arrival, 10 minutes of easy mobility and elevate the legs. Protect sleep hard tonight; adaptation from the strength session happens while you're down.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Peak phase rewards the athlete who trains anywhere. You're moving countries and still stacking a run and a strength block — that's the exact consistency that shows up on a Slovenian ridge in September. The Julian Alps won't care that you were mid-travel; they'll reward the durability you're building right now. Nail the small day. Discipline on the easy ones is what earns the big ones.
